trackIdentity.legalName: Expungement or Sealing Following a Prisoner Review Board Certificate of Eligibility
trackIdentity.publicName: Using a Prisoner Review Board certificate to clear a record that is otherwise excluded
trackIdentity.compositionModeNote: The registry records compositionMode "mixed". The route is sequential across two stages before two different bodies (agency, then court) and alternative within stage 1 across three mutually exclusive certificate branches, one of which is unavailable. Units 2, 3 and 4 are the alternative branches under parent unit 1; unit 5 is sequential after whichever branch produced a certificate.
trackIdentity.outputStrategyNote: Null at track level by design for a composed track; each unit carries its own. Every available unit carries outputStrategy official_pdf_fill, so this route drafts no pleading document at all — see filingSeparation and the dependency components.

reliefVocabulary.primaryReliefTermsBasis: This track is genuinely both, and the split is legally load-bearing. § 5.2(e-5) is a certificate of eligibility for SEALING; § 5.2(e-6) is a certificate of eligibility for EXPUNGEMENT. The registry records them as legally distinct and the branch a participant takes is set by which certificate the Board issues. The stage-2 Request form carries checkboxes for expunge versus seal and the per-case election is an express manual completion item.
prohibitedUsage: Never present the military Certificate of Expungement as a general certificate-of-expungement application. It is military-specific.
Never treat a § 5.2(e-5) sealing certificate and a § 5.2(e-6) expungement certificate as interchangeable.
Never make the expunge-versus-seal election for the participant. The registry records it as a legal judgment the review expressly bars from auto-completion.
Never say a record will be sealed automatically before January 1, 2029 (profile copyGuardrails[4]); Clean Slate automatic sealing phases in through 2034.
Never promise erasure, sealing, eligibility, timing, filing acceptance, or a court or Board outcome (profile copyGuardrails[7]).

provenance.profileCoverageNote: The compiled IL profile records no pathway, question, ordered decision rule, waiting-period rule, exclusion rule or packetGenerator entry for il-prb-cert. Its nine pathways are adult non-conviction expungement, expungement after supervision or qualified probation, adult conviction sealing, cannabis, human-trafficking survivor, felony prostitution, criminal identity theft, juvenile, and Clean Slate automatic sealing. Full-value scans return zero hits for "5.2(e-5)", "5.2(e-6)", "5.2(d)(2)", "certificate of eligibility" and "Certificate of Sealing". The profile mentions the Prisoner Review Board only four times and only in the cannabis-pardon context, not the certificate-of-eligibility context — see omissionProof. Unit enumeration therefore comes entirely from the pinned registry entry; the profile supplies the stage-2 form suite, the ISP Access-and-Review record-gathering step, the fee narrative, the terminology and the copy guardrails.

mechanism: Two stages before two different bodies. The petitioner first applies to the Prisoner Review Board for a certificate of eligibility for sealing under § 5.2(e-5) or for expungement under § 5.2(e-6); that is discretionary agency relief outside the circuit court. With the certificate attached under § 5.2(d)(2), the petitioner then files in the circuit court under the same venue formula as the pardon route.

The Board's own procedural rules, cited throughout the registry entry as the source for the acknowledgement-first rule, the required narratives, the notarised perjury declaration, the supporting-documentation list, the 75-day filing deadline, the proof-of-delivery requirement and the four-year bar after a denial.

destination.detail: Stage 1 is an agency application. Stage 2 is a court petition with the certificate attached.

screeningKeys.question: In which Illinois county were you convicted?
Has the Prisoner Review Board already issued you a certificate of eligibility?
Is the certificate one for sealing or one for expungement?
screeningKeys.conditionDescription: Asked only where a certificate has been issued, because it selects § 5.2(e-5) or § 5.2(e-6).

screeningKeys.question: Is your offense on the § 5.2(a)(3) exclusion list, so that ordinary sealing is unavailable?
Are you seeking the certificate on the basis of military service?
Have you petitioned the Prisoner Review Board for a certificate of sealing before, and if so when?
Have you ever petitioned for executive clemency, and if so in what month and year was it considered?
In your own words, give your personal life history: date and place of birth, education, employment, marital status, and whether you served in the military.
In your own words, why are you seeking this certificate?
In your own words, describe the facts of the offence including dates, places and surrounding circumstances.

units.legalUnit: Stage 1 — the Prisoner Review Board certificate application stage. The participant applies to the Board for a certificate of eligibility. Which certificate depends on the branch selected below. Board discretion, the rehabilitation narrative, notarisation, supporting documents and a possible Board hearing are filing instructions and post-generation conditions, not reasons to withhold a packet. This unit is the parent framing and branch-selection unit; it produces no filing of its own.

omissionProof.statement: units[] enumerates every legal unit that the pinned registry entry and the IL state pack record for il-prb-cert, and adds no unit either source does not record. It is a one-to-one mapping of registry@3b6f4c1:tracks[142].units[0..4], preserving their unitIds, order values and parentUnitId relationships exactly: il-prb-cert-certificate-application (order 1, parent, resolved, available), il-prb-cert-sealing-branch (order 2, parent=1, resolved, available), il-prb-cert-military-branch (order 3, parent=1, resolved, available), il-prb-cert-nonmilitary-expungement-branch (order 4, parent=1, outputStrategyStatus unresolved, available false), il-prb-cert-court-petition (order 5, resolved, available). No sixth unit exists. registry packetSet.components contains exactly five entries, and all five are carried: components[0] and [1] on unit 2, components[2] and [3] on unit 3, components[4] on unit 5. Unit 1 has no registry component because the registry treats it as parent framing, and unit 4 has none because the registry generates no packet for it; both were given constructed componentIds and both are recorded as constructed. Nothing in packetSet.participantActionRequired constitutes a separate legal unit: its thirty-one entries are participant acts against units 2, 3 and 5 — nine obtain_document and confirm_answer pairs for record gathering, seven complete_field manual completion items, one sign, one notarize, one pay_fee, one apply_fee_waiver, one serve_party and one file — and every one of them is carried inside the stage-1 orientation component, the dependency files, or participant-instructions.md. registry postGenerationHandoffs is empty, so no unit is drawn from it. registry manualCompletionItems has seven entries, all of which map onto units 2, 3 and 5 rather than describing separate units. No agency_request_letter unit and no cover_sheet unit is created; the registry records no written request document and no cover sheet, and creating either would exceed the source.

profilePassageReferenced.passage: ISP identifies eligible minor cannabis conviction records and forwards them to the Prisoner Review Board for the Governors pardon-and-expungement process. If a pardon authorizing expungement is granted, the PRB through the Attorney General files a petition in the circuit where the conviction occurred. Individuals may also file a motion to vacate and expunge certain misdemeanor or Class 4 felony cannabis convictions under 5.2(i)(3).
profilePassageReferenced.interpretation: This is one of only four passages in the entire compiled IL profile that mention the Prisoner Review Board, and all four are in the cannabis-pardon context inside pathways[3] (cannabis-specific automatic or petition expungement) — a different track (il-cannabis-auto / il-exp-pardon). The Board appears there as a conduit for the Governor's pardon-and-expungement process, not as the issuer of a § 5.2(e-5) or § 5.2(e-6) certificate of eligibility. Full-value scans of the profile return zero hits for "5.2(e-5)", "5.2(e-6)", "5.2(d)(2)", "certificate of eligibility" and "Certificate of Sealing". The compiled profile therefore records ZERO legal units for il-prb-cert, and the enumeration above cannot be a subset of it — it is a complete image of the registry's own units[]. What the profile does supply, and what is used here, is stage-2 context: sourceSections[2] and [20] enumerate the mandatory statewide adult suite that unit 5 depends on (Request, Case List, Notice of Filing, Order, Denial order, Certificate of Service by Circuit Clerk, Fee Waiver Application) and record that all Illinois courts must accept them; sourceSections[10] supplies the ISP Access-and-Review record-gathering step and the Chicago RAP-sheet caveat; sourceSections[11] and [23] supply the fee narrative; and terminology plus copyGuardrails supply the vocabulary rules.

counselFlags.statement: No official non-military certificate-of-eligibility-for-expungement application under § 5.2(e-6) has been located on the Prisoner Review Board site. The Board publishes a Certificate of Sealing and a military-specific Certificate of Expungement. Unit il-prb-cert-nonmilitary-expungement-branch is blocked and nothing is drafted for it. A non-military participant seeking expungement rather than sealing has no route on this track.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether an official non-military § 5.2(e-6) application exists; if it does not, what the Board actually accepts from a non-military petitioner seeking an expungement certificate, and whether that is a legal-design question rather than a form-acquisition question.

counselFlags.statement: The military branch must never be presented as a general certificate-of-expungement application. It is military-specific, and a § 5.2(e-5) sealing certificate and a § 5.2(e-6) expungement certificate remain legally distinct. The failure mode is a non-military participant being routed onto the military form because it is the only expungement-certificate form that exists.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That routing logic hard-blocks the military application for any participant whose eligibility does not rest on military service, and that the blocked non-military branch does not silently fall through to it.

counselFlags.statement: Zero pleading documents are drafted on this route. All four available components and the stage-2 filing are official_pdf_fill, and the stage-2 statewide suite is mandatory — the Illinois Supreme Court Commission on Access to Justice approved the adult forms and all Illinois courts must accept them. Drafting a bespoke pleading at either stage would be affirmatively wrong.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no downstream lane substitutes a drafted document for any of the five official forms named in filingSeparation.

counselFlags.statement: The Certificate of Sealing Acknowledgement and the military Eligibility Acknowledgement carry no visible revision dates. Both are published undated alongside dated 09/18/2024 application and guideline files. Separately, the acknowledgement-first rejection rule is recorded on the Certificate of Sealing Guidelines; whether the military acknowledgement carries the same rejection consequence is not separately stated.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The revision date of each acknowledgement form, and whether the military acknowledgement must likewise be completed before the application on pain of rejection.

counselFlags.statement: County filing fees statewide are unresolved. Published examples run from roughly $60 to $235 and there is no statewide schedule. The registry records ISP as charging nothing to file a petition and $60 to process a court order, and McLean County as publishing $136; the compiled profile breaks that $136 down as $60 filing plus $60 ISP plus $16 for four certified copies, and records a Cook County single-fee-per-day rule across districts. No fee figure of any kind is printed in this route.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Build a county fee table before any fee figure is shown to a participant. Treat every published figure as county-specific.

counselFlags.statement: Whether e-filing is available for expungement and sealing petitions in every county, and how counties handle self-represented e-filing exemptions, is unresolved. The compiled profile records that copy counts, e-filing rules and mailing procedures differ by county and that petitioners should call the clerk first.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Per-county e-filing availability and the self-represented exemption route, before any filing-method instruction is given for stage 2.

counselFlags.statement: Stage 1 is a self-help stop condition always. The certificate application is a discretionary rehabilitation case and is not suitable for an automated template. Any objection or contested hearing at stage 2 is likewise a stop condition, and a Board hearing is a post-generation event requiring referral. The Office of the State Appellate Defender, Expungement Unit, 866-787-1776, is the statewide referral destination for every stop condition.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the referral is presented at stage 1 by default rather than only on failure, given that the whole of stage 1 is a stop condition while still being packet-capable.

counselFlags.statement: The facts-of-the-offence statement, the personal life history and the reasons for seeking the certificate are participant-authored through structured prompts. LegalEase formats the participant's own words and never composes the rehabilitation showing. Perjury on the sworn declaration is a Class 3 felony punishable by up to 10 years, so nothing generated may end up sworn to.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the narrative prompts capture the participant's own words verbatim and that no generated, summarised or suggested language reaches a sworn field.

counselFlags.statement: Notarisation is required before filing: the declaration that all assertions are complete, truthful and accurate must be signed and sworn before a notary public. The witness or attorney signature on the acknowledgement is third-party completed and LegalEase leaves it blank.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the notarisation and third-party-signature blocks are surfaced as manual completion items on every stage-1 branch, and that neither is ever prefilled.

counselFlags.statement: Stage-1 filing mechanics are exacting and are quoted rather than paraphrased: mail or deliver the original petition to the Board at 1001 North Walnut Street, Springfield, Illinois 62702; staple or clip the pages so they can be separated, do not bind them or use plastic sleeves; the completed petition must be received at least 75 days before the first date of the hearing schedule to be considered on that docket; and proof of delivery to the sentencing or chief judge and to the current State's Attorney of the county of conviction must be demonstrated to the Board, by notarised affidavit or otherwise.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the 75-day deadline is computed against a Board hearing schedule the participant has actually looked up, and what form of proof of delivery the Board accepts.

counselFlags.statement: No petition will be accepted for review within four years of the denial of a prior petition for the same individual, unless the Chairman permits an exception for compelling reasons. priorPrbPetition is a required screening key precisely because of this bar. Whether the four years runs from the denial date or from some other date, and what counts as compelling, is not stated.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: How the four-year bar is computed and how a participant inside the window is routed, including whether the Chairman's exception is worth attempting.

counselFlags.statement: The expunge-versus-seal election for each case at stage 2 is a legal judgment the review expressly bars from auto-completion. It is a manual completion item on the Case List's per-case election column. The two remedies are not interchangeable and a record is usually eligible for one or the other, not both.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the per-case election is never auto-filled, never defaulted, and never inferred from certificateType, and that the participant is told what turns on the choice.

counselFlags.statement: The stage-2 hearing date is a manual completion item: the court sets a hearing only if an objection is filed, with at least 30 days' notice. Objections come from the State's Attorney, the arresting agency, the chief legal officer of the arresting unit of local government and the Illinois State Police, who generally have 60 days to object; agencies may then have up to 60 days to process an order. None of that is asserted or predicted anywhere in this route.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the objection window and the post-order processing window are stated to the participant as ranges rather than commitments, and that no document asserts an objection, a hearing, or an outcome.
